title: Christmas Outfit Ideas: Indian Ethnic Wear for Women (2026)
excerpt: Eight Indian ethnic outfit ideas for Christmas, from a sage taffeta Anarkali for dinner to a simple kurti for Christmas Eve, with styling tips.
body:
The best Indian ethnic outfits for Christmas are a gota work Anarkali for dinner, an embroidered kurta set for family lunch, and a simple embroidered kurti for the relaxed days in between. Pick colours that glow under fairy lights, such as sage green, purple, rani pink and winter white, and keep your layers in mind if you live somewhere cold.

*By the Bahe Kurtiz styling team, Jaipur. We hand embroider and hand block print in our own Jaipur unit, and stitch every piece there.*

**Quick answer**

- Christmas dinner: a taffeta or chiffon Anarkali with a sheer dupatta
- Christmas morning or brunch: an off-white or pastel embroidered kurta set
- Christmas Eve at home: an embroidered kurti with jeans or palazzos
- Church service: a kurta set with a dupatta you can drape over your shoulders
- The day after Christmas: a tunic top, jeans and a long cardigan

## What are the best Indian outfits for Christmas?

Christmas is a long celebration, not a single evening. You might have a quiet Christmas Eve, a big family meal, a church visit and a slow day after. These eight looks cover the whole stretch, so you can plan once and enjoy the days.

### 1. Sage green taffeta Anarkali for Christmas dinner

Green is the colour of the season, and sage is a softer, more modern way to wear it. The [sage green taffeta silk Anarkali with sequin organza dupatta](/products/sage-green-taffeta-silk-gota-work-anarkali-suit-set-with-sequin-organza-dupatta/) has gota work that catches candlelight beautifully. Add gold earrings and keep the rest simple.

### 2. Purple bandhani Anarkali for a party night

Bandhani brings a playful, tie-dye texture that looks lovely in photos. The [purple bandhani chiffon Anarkali with hand-embroidered neckline](/products/purple-bandhani-chiffon-anarkali-suit-set/) is light and flowing, so it is easy to wear for a long evening.

Our guide on [what bandhani is](/blog/what-is-bandhani-how-to-style-a-bandhani-anarkali/) explains how this craft works.

### 3. Off-white kurta set for Christmas morning

Winter white feels fresh and calm on Christmas morning, especially with a red lip or a pop of colour in your jewellery. The [off-white embroidered cotton kurta set with cutwork organza dupatta](/products/off-white-embroidered-cotton-flex-kurta-pant-organza-dupatta-set/) is soft enough for brunch and opening presents, yet smart enough for photos.

### 4. Rani pink kurti for Christmas Eve at home

Christmas Eve is often cosy, with films, baking and wrapping. A [rani pink embroidered kurti with side tie-up](/products/rani-pink-embroidered-kurti/) over jeans or palazzos looks bright and festive without trying too hard. Rani pink also works as a warm alternative if you do not own red.

### 5. Coral chanderi kurta set for a family lunch

Coral is warm and cheerful, and chanderi has a gentle sheen that suits daylight. It is a good choice for a long lunch where you sit at the table for hours. Add a bold bindi and gold bangles.

### 6. Plum embroidered suit for the church service

Plum is rich and quiet, which makes it a good fit for a midnight or morning service. A kurta, pants and dupatta set lets you drape the dupatta over your shoulders when you need to.

### 7. Navy kota doria set for a day out

If you are heading to a Christmas market, a light kota doria kurta set under a long coat feels comfortable and looks polished. Navy hides the little marks that come with a busy day.

### 8. Tunic top and jeans for the day after

The day after Christmas is for leftovers and walks. A cotton tunic top with jeans and a long cardigan is relaxed and still a little desi. Browse our [cotton tunic tops](/cotton-tunic-tops-short-kurtis-for-jeans/) for easy options at a gentle price.

## Which look should I wear for which part of Christmas?

| Moment | Look | Fabric | Why it works |
|---|---|---|---|
| Christmas dinner | Taffeta or chiffon Anarkali | Taffeta silk, chiffon | Shine and volume for the main event |
| Christmas morning | Embroidered kurta set | Cotton with organza dupatta | Soft, smart and photo-ready |
| Christmas Eve | Embroidered kurti with jeans | Cotton | Festive but relaxed |
| Church service | Kurta set with dupatta | Cotton, chanderi | Covered shoulders, easy to sit in |
| Day after Christmas | Tunic top with jeans | Cotton | Comfortable for walks and visits |

## How do I make Indian outfits work in a cold Christmas?

If you live in the UK, Canada or the northern USA, plan for two temperatures: cold outside and warm inside. Wear a long coat that covers the length of your kurta, so the hem does not peek out unevenly. Thin thermal leggings fit under most pants and palazzos.

A wool shawl in a neutral colour, such as camel or grey, works with nearly every outfit on this list. Carry your juttis or flats and change at the door. In Australia, where Christmas falls in summer, skip the layers and pick cotton and chanderi for daytime events.

> **From our Jaipur studio:** Taffeta silk holds its shape well, so the flare of an Anarkali looks full even after hours of sitting. Chiffon and georgette are softer and drape closer to the body. If you want a dramatic twirl in photos, taffeta gives you more volume.

## Our pick for you

If you only buy one piece, make it the sage green taffeta Anarkali for dinner. Add the off-white kurta set for the morning, and the rani pink kurti for the quieter days. Undecided between plum and violet shades? Our post on [plum vs violet kurta sets](/blog/purple-kurta-sets-for-diwali-plum-vs-violet/) compares the two.

A small note: if you are a guest at someone else's Christmas, match their level of dressiness, and bring a little something for the table.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can I wear Indian ethnic wear on Christmas Day?**
Yes. Many Indian families abroad wear ethnic outfits for Christmas lunch or dinner. Choose a festive kurta set or Anarkali, and keep a coat handy if it is cold.

**What colour should I wear for Christmas if I don't want red?**
Try sage green, bottle green, rani pink, plum or winter white. These feel festive and look rich under warm indoor lights.

**Is an Anarkali too dressy for a family Christmas?**
Not for dinner. An Anarkali is perfect for the main meal. For a casual lunch or Christmas Eve, a kurta set or kurti is easier.

**How do I wash a taffeta or chiffon Anarkali after the party?**
We suggest dry cleaning for taffeta silk and chiffon pieces with gota or embroidery. Store them folded in a cotton bag, away from damp.
